newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eramet hopeful as N. Caledonia talks star.
newsitem.headline: Eramet hopeful as N. Caledonia talks star.

text.p: Eramet said on Friday it hoped a solution could be worked out over a controversial plan to build a new nickel smelter in New Caledonia.
But the company said it regretted recent criticisms made by its main shareholder, state-owned holding Erap, against the management of Eramet, calling them "excessive" and "not accurate".
The president of Eramet is meeting today in Paris the presidents of Canadian group Falconbridge and Societe de Sud Pacifique (SMSP) to discuss the plan.
"We are going to the talks in a spirit of good will and determined to find a solution," a company spokesman said.
"But we regret recent attacks against Eramet's management that were excessive, often not accurate and raised doubt over Eramet's ability to make progress in the negotiations," he said.
On Wednesday Remy Chardon, the chairman of Erap, criticised the way Eramet's managers had handled a long-standing dispute over the distribution of mining assets in the French territory.
"In this affair we blame Eramet's managers for having wasted an ernormous amount of time," Chardon told French daily La Tribune.

Eramet has repeatedly said it was supporting plans by Falconbridge and local Kanak company SMPS to build a nickel plant in the north of the South Pacific island as long as it did not threaten its development stategy in New Caledonia.
Government supports the plan as it is part of a deal to appease local Kanak separatists ahead of a 1998 referendum on independence for the island.
The spokesman said the talks were expected to focus on an initial plan to swap mining assets between Eramet's Societe le Nickel and SMSP.
Under the plan Falconbridge and SMSP would get the right to use Eramet's Koniambo field to supply ore to their plant and Eramet would obtain the rights to the Poum field.
Eramet has said it was not opposed to the exchange as long as it was fair and Eramet would get sufficient compensation for the exchange.
The meeting should also shed light on Falconbrige's plans in New Caledonia, notably the cost of the smelter.
